adversarial_probes.name: R-1 live: corrupt clearance marker on a read grant
adversarial_probes.setup: read grant with constraint.clearance = 'ultrasecret' (not a member of the closed DataClass set), effective at NOW
adversarial_probes.observed: sensitive_read === false, level === 'routine' (UNDER-flag). deriveClearance -> readClearanceMarker -> isDataClass rejects the garbage token to null, so axis c stays false. Monotonicity holds: a corrupt-clearance read grant does NOT clear a sibling real 'confidential' read grant in the same set (bit stays true).
adversarial_probes.for_T-0044: Per-task NF-3 'doubt -> MORE criticality' is monotone-EXACT for axes a/b (an OR-fold .some() can only fail to RAISE, never lower), but axis c inherits T-0033 deriveClearance's quiet-null: a corrupt clearance token resolves to null rather than to the maximal class, so a garbage clearance marker under-flags rather than over-flags. Spec-conformant (FR-4/AC-8 define the bit via deriveClearance yielding a DataClass; 'no resolvable clearance marker => false'). Fixing would require editing the FROZEN T-0033 deriveClearance (out of scope, forbidden by NF-5). Cross-task seam for T-0044/T-0033: if a corrupt clearance marker should ELEVATE criticality, that is a clearance-corruption-signal design question on the join, not a T-0040 contract-boundary defect. Confirms reviewer nit R-1 factually.

adversarial_probes.name: expired approve window + effective confidential read
adversarial_probes.setup: one approve grant on an EXPIRED window (validUntil = NOW-1) + one effective read grant conferring 'confidential'
adversarial_probes.observed: { approve_or_transition: false, external_invoke: false, sensitive_read: true, level: 'critical' }
adversarial_probes.verdict: pass — matches expected {a:false, c:true}; effective-window gate (FR-6) correctly drops the expired approve, the live confidential read raises axis c, any-bit => critical

adversarial_probes.name: criticalityDiff escalation direction (contract §5)
adversarial_probes.setup: none -> {c} (confidential read added), then {c} -> {a,c} (approve added on top)
adversarial_probes.observed: none->{c}: escalates=true, expanded={a:false,b:false,c:true} (routine->critical step). {c}->{a,c}: expanded.approve_or_transition=true (newly held), expanded.sensitive_read=false (already held, not an expansion), escalates=false (already critical => no routine->critical step).
adversarial_probes.verdict: pass — 'raising' direction consistent with §5: escalates keys ONLY on routine->critical; a within-critical bit addition expands that bit but does not re-escalate

adversarial_probes.name: 10k-grant fold performance smoke (no quadratic blowup)
adversarial_probes.setup: 10000 grants (mostly internal-only reads + a sprinkle of effect-invoke and approve), single combineCriticality call
adversarial_probes.observed: 1.44ms; output correct (a:true, b:true, c:false (all reads internal), level:'critical'). Linear-fold cost; well under a loose 250ms ceiling.
adversarial_probes.verdict: pass — fold is linear in grant count (filter + .some + .filter + deriveClearance loop), no O(n^2) behaviour

adversarial_probes.name: combineCriticality([]) neutral element
adversarial_probes.observed: { approve_or_transition: false, external_invoke: false, sensitive_read: false, level: 'routine' } (deep-equal)
adversarial_probes.verdict: pass — empty input is the identity/neutral element of the criticality fold (all axes false, routine)
